source.label: thm:lower_bound
source.quote: For any given $\alpha, K, T$ and (possibly randomized) policy $\pi$, there exists an instance $\phi$ of problem \eqref{eq:regret} with $K+1$ arms such that $    \qreg_\pi(T, \alpha, \phi) + \creg_\pi(T,\alpha,\phi) $ is  $ \Omega\left((1-\alpha)^2 K^{\frac{1}{3}}T^{\frac{2}{3}}\right)$ when $0 \leq \alpha \leq 1$ and  $1 \leq K \leq T$.

results.notes: Bound on sum of quality and cost regret. Instance has K+1 arms.

source.label: lem:alpha_0_neat
source.quote: For any given $p, K, T$ and any (possibly randomized) policy $\pi$, there exists an instance $\phi$ (from the family $\cIzero$) such that $\qreg_{\pi}(T, 0,\phi) + \creg_{\pi}(T, 0,\phi)$ is $\Omega\left( pK^{\frac{1}{3}}T^{\frac{2}{3}} \right)$ when $0 < p \leq 1/2$ and $1 \leq  K \leq T$.

results.notes: Special case alpha=0 used to prove Theorem 2; expression depends on instance-family parameter p.

source.label: thm:explore_first_regret
source.quote: For an instance $\phi$ with $K$ arms, when  the number of exploration pulls of each arm $ \tau = (T/K)^{2/3}$, then the sum of cost and quality regret incurred by \mainALG \  (Algorithm \ref{alg:explore_first}) on any instance $\phi$ i.e. $\qreg_{\mainALG}(T, \alpha,  \phi) + \creg_{\mainALG}(T, \alpha, \phi)$ is $O(K^{1/3}T^{2/3}\sqrt{\log{T}})$.

results.notes: Bound on sum of quality and cost regret. Paper states (informally, Section 5.2) that the same bound holds for a modified CS-ETC with unknown random costs in [0,1].

tuning: confidence width sqrt(2 log T / T_i(t))

source.label: thm:cost_quality_consistent
source.quote: If for an instance $\phi$ with $K$ arms,  $|c_i - c_j| \leq \delta |\mu_i - \mu_j| \ \forall i, j \in [K]$ and any (possibly unknown) $\delta >0$, then $\qreg_{\consUCB}(T, \alpha,  \phi) + \creg_{\consUCB}(T, \alpha, \phi)$ is $O((1+\delta) \sqrt{KT \log{T}})$.

results.notes: Paper's delta (consistency constant) renamed delta_cons. Paper says the bound also holds for a modified CS-UCB with unknown costs.
